alignment.note: Greek opens with the feminine article ἡ functioning quasi-pronominally with γυνή; the Peshitta similarly fronts the demonstrative/pronoun ܗܝ. The Vulgate omits any article (Latin lacking the category), beginning directly with Mulier.
δέ / ܕܝܢ / vero — the postpositive adversative-continuative particle is rendered consistently across all three traditions.
γυνή / ܐܢܬܬܐ / Mulier.

Greek uses a single aorist passive participle φοβηθεῖσα ('having been frightened'); the Peshitta renders this with the temporal subordinator ܟܕ ('when') plus the adjectival/participial ܕܚܝܠܐ, an analytic construction. The Vulgate present participle timens is semantically equivalent.
καί / et coordinating the two participles; the Peshitta expresses the coordination with the proclitic waw prefixed to ܘܪܬܝܬܐ rather than a discrete token.
τρέμουσα / ܘܪܬܝܬܐ / tremens.

Greek perfect active participle εἰδυῖα is matched by the Vulgate present participle sciens. The Peshitta ܕܝܕܥܬ employs a relative/finite verbal form (perfect 3fs with proclitic d-), shifting the participial syntax to a subordinate verbal clause.
ὅ / ܡܐ / quod, the neuter relative introducing the content clause.

Greek perfect γέγονεν ('has happened') is rendered by the Peshitta perfect ܕܗܘܐ. The Vulgate uses a periphrastic pluperfect subjunctive factum esset, reflecting Latin sequence-of-tenses within the indirect statement rather than a simple perfect.

Greek ἐπ᾽ αὐτῇ ('upon her') and Vulgate in se use a preposition plus pronoun. The Peshitta condenses this to the single dative-marked enclitic ܠܗ ('to/for her'), a more economical idiomatic rendering of the affected person.
ἦλθεν / ܐܬܬ / venit.
καί / et joining the two finite verbs; the Peshitta omits an explicit conjunction here, juxtaposing ܐܬܬ ܢܦܠܬ asyndetically, a common Syriac narrative idiom.
προσέπεσεν / ܢܦܠܬ / procidit.

Greek uses a bare dative αὐτῷ ('to/before him') with προσπίπτω; the Vulgate makes the spatial relation explicit with the preposition ante eum ('before him'). The Peshitta likewise uses the prepositional ܩܕܡܘܗܝ ('before him'), agreeing with the Latin against the Greek simple dative.
καί / et; the Peshitta encodes the coordination with the waw proclitic on ܘܐܡܪܬ rather than as a separate token.
εἶπεν / ܘܐܡܪܬ / dixit.
αὐτῷ / ܠܗ / ei, the dative indirect object of the verb of speaking.
πᾶσαν / ܟܠܗ / omnem.

Greek includes the definite article τήν with ἀλήθειαν. Neither the Peshitta (where definiteness is carried by the emphatic-state noun ܫܪܪܐ) nor the Vulgate (which lacks articles) attests a separate article token.
ἀλήθειαν / ܫܪܪܐ / veritatem; the Greek paragraph marker (¶) is editorial and carries no textual weight.
